routeSelection.basis: The generic target contains three current specialisations. International Economics and Policy covers economic theory, international markets, sustainability, inequality and policy and therefore best represents the degree’s broad academic economics identity. Accounting and Finance are more sector-specific; this choice was made from Radboud’s stated programme, independent of UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics and Business Economics studies economic decisions, firms, financial markets and societal policy. The displayed International Economics and Policy specialization combines economic theory, quantitative research, business finance and policy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The published credit structure is shown while the thesis-entry conditions for the renewed curriculum are clarified. UCR comparisons are withheld pending that clarification.

curriculum.routeLabel: International Economics and Policy; renewed curriculum for 2025 entrants
curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 180 EC, but the prerequisite relationship for the required thesis remains unresolved. This is a supported credit structure rather than a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y3-electives: 24 EC of approved choice, normally 18 EC in period 1 and 6 EC in period 4. Courses outside the programme require approval and must not overlap. Master’s and applied-sciences courses are normally excluded; exceptions for study abroad follow the approved learning agreement. An optional 12 EC internship may replace two 6 EC electives.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 12 EC economics research project. The formal entry rule names earlier methods courses whose relationship to the renewed curriculum needs authoritative clarification.
componentNotes.y1-academic: Academic and professional skills are compulsory. The linked academic-language test adds no credits. First-year study advice normally requires 42 of 60 EC, with personal circumstances considered.
